posts.title: The Riemann hypothesis: what next for Lean?
posts.description: Now that we've finished the "let's check the Lean proof carefully" stage, and there are essentially no remaining doubts as to whether this is a correct proof, let's get organized making sure Lean is as useful as possible during the next stage of humans acquiring understanding of the proof. This will surely proceed in several directions.

posts.title: An error in the Isabelle/HOL formalization of sheaves
posts.description: The AFP entry Grothendieck's Schemes in Algebraic Geometry states the sheaf axioms only for covers indexed by sets of real numbers. As a consequence, the predicate sheaf_of_rings accepts a presheaf that fails gluing. posts.title: Computational permutation groups in Lean
posts.description: Hex now has a perm_group tactic, which uses the Schreier-Sims algorithm to answer many questions about permutation groups. Here we calculate the order of the Mathieu group M11 (defined as a group generated by two permutations). HexPermGroup contains the tactic, and HexPermGroupTheory contains additional glue that teaches the tactic how to work with Mathlib's permutations.
